summary: I fixed the bug in `solution/core.py`, and both visible tests now pass. The problem was the line that merges overlapping intervals: it always set the new end to the incoming interval's end, `(pa, b)`. When an interval sat fully inside the previous one, the merged result got shorter — `(1, 4)` plus `(2, 3)` came out as `(1, 3)`, and `(1, 3)` plus the point `(2, 2)` came out as `(1, 2)`. I changed it to keep whichever end is larger, `(pa, max(pb, b))`, so a contained interval or point can no longer cut the merged range short. Beyond the tests, I ran a few quick cases by hand: several intervals nested in one, containment followed by an interval that just touches, with `join_touching` both on and off, and intervals sharing a start point. All gave the expected results. I didn't change anything else.
